title: Plan graph (plan.yaml)
description: Machine-readable, immutable structure of a plan emitted by mplan: waves, stories, dependencies, and per-story validation. Lives at context/project/plans/<plan-id>/plan.yaml, alongside the human-readable PLAN-*.md story files and the mutable state.yaml. mexecute reads this instead of re-deriving structure from prose.

version.description: New plans are written with 4. 4 declares a graph continuously checked: it carries waves[].validation, the barrier check run against the merged integration branch. 3 declares a graph slice-bearing but checked only at its story and slice boundaries — the delivery model it was written for. A 1 or 2 graph carries no slices and is read as one implicit slice containing every wave, which is the delivery model those were written for — no pre-existing plan needs migrating. The version, not the presence of a key, is the discriminator at every step: sniffing for slices would let a malformed version-3 graph silently degrade to whole-job delivery, and making the version-4 keys optional on 3 would let a graph omit the very checks that version exists to require and still validate.

plan_id.description: <NNN>-<slug>, matching the plan directory name, e.g. 003-adapter-retry-logic or 000-initial.

project_change.description: The PROJECT-CHANGE <NNN> this plan implements; null for a full/greenfield plan. Quote the value in YAML — an unquoted digit run resolves as a number (e.g. 010 becomes the integer 8 under YAML 1.1's octal branch), which fails the string type.

repos.description: Every repo this plan touches (one story targets exactly one repo).

slices.description: The delivery axis: each entry is the set of stories that make one behaviour run end to end. Required when version is 3, forbidden below it. Two producer obligations JSON Schema cannot express are checked by mc.py instead: every story appears in exactly one slice, and at least one acceptance step of every slice is kind: exit-code.

validation.description: The barrier check: run against the merged integration branch after this wave's greens land and before the next wave is cut from it. Required when version is 4, forbidden below it. This is the only point at which stories built in isolated worktrees are exercised together — mplan guarantees same-wave stories write disjoint paths, which makes the merge conflict-free but says nothing about whether the merged behaviour holds. At least one step must be kind: exit-code, which mc.py checks, since JSON Schema cannot.

storyId.description: {WW}-{SS}[m]-{REPO}-{MODULE}, matching the PLAN-*.md filename minus the PLAN- prefix and .md suffix.

sliceId.description: Zero-padded slice number; 00 is the walking skeleton.

behavior.description: The one behaviour this slice makes run end to end.

acceptance.description: The runnable demonstration that the behaviour works. At least one step must be kind: exit-code — a slice whose acceptance is prose alone forces a human stop under every gate policy but never — which mc.py checks, since JSON Schema cannot.

stories.description: The stories delivered in this slice; the back-reference each story's slice field is checked against.

kind.description: exit-code steps are runnable commands (preferred); prose steps are agent-interpreted.

command.description: Required when kind is exit-code: a shell command run relative to repos/<repo>/ that must exit 0.

slice.description: The slice this story belongs to. Required alongside version: 3 by the same if/then pair that requires slices, and forbidden below it.

prerequisites.description: Story ids from earlier waves that must be applied first. Empty for wave 1.

parallel_group.description: Same-wave sibling stories that run concurrently. Module-disjoint by construction.

change_file.description: Incremental plans: the repo-level change file this story implements. null for full/greenfield.

target_paths.description: Source paths (relative to repos/<repo>/) this story writes — used to confirm module-disjointness.
